title: Container Bookings: The Desk's Entries and the Shipper's Declarations on a Live Booking
content:
A live Container Bookings booking accumulates two sorts of record: entries on its charge account, and the documents the line receives for the sailing it is allocated to. This page names the charge-account entries the desk writes and the declaration the shipper supplies itself, and it describes how the records made in one handling relate to the booking and when they take effect.

## Entries made by the desk

Several kinds of charge-account entry are written by the desk: fees for changes the customer asked for, goodwill waivers, compensation the line owes for a roll the carrier caused, and entries for documents that reached the line after their cut-off but within grace, whether shipping instructions or a verified gross mass (VGM). Each entry is made on the terms, and at the amount, that the rule governing that kind of entry lays down; this page adds nothing to those rules.

## Declarations made by the shipper

The VGM is a declaration for which the shipper is responsible. Its transmission to the line is carried out by the customer themselves, using a tool that belongs to the customer; the desk never sends a VGM on the shipper's behalf.

## One booking throughout

Whatever is recorded in a single handling attaches to the booking under handling: credits and late entries go onto that booking's charge account, and a transmitted declaration is recorded against that same booking.

## Effect and completion

Each record takes effect at the moment it is made, inside the consultation; none of them has to wait for goods to move, for someone to review it, for money to arrive or for time to pass. The handling of the booking is complete once each of those desk entries that is due on the booking stands on its account in the form and at the amount its own rule prescribes, and any VGM the shipper has transmitted stands recorded as received for the allocated sailing.
